## REQ-MSG-001

**Payload objects are not extended by user-defined keys**

A sender is strict: the payload objects of MG 8 (NetworkMessage, DataSetMessage, DataSetMetaData and their sub-objects, Action messages, OI4 resources) contain only keys defined for them by the guideline or by OPC UA for the respective structure; fields marked "Not used" are omitted. The DataSet in the Payload of a DataSetMessage is the only place for publisher-defined names.

- Keyword: MUST NOT
- Levels: L1 MUST NOT · L2 MUST NOT · L3 MUST NOT
- Domain: messaging · Applies to: publisher, requester, responder
- Refs: MG 8, MG 8.2, SF-050, SF-052
- Verification: schema, d7-validate
- Status: reviewed
- Inventory: MG-8-ea83c386, MG-8.2-20499c7b, MG-8.2-490014d6, MG-8.2-674a78a9

> The objects defined in this chapter must not be extended by user defined keys, i.e. keys that are defined neither by OPC UA nor by this guideline (8.2 OPC UA Objects - Defined by OPC Foundation): a sender is strict in what it sends.
> — MG 8

> Fields that OPC UA defines for these structures, but that are not listed in this chapter, are allowed and follow the OPC UA specifications; they are no user defined keys (8 Payload Format).
> — MG 8.2

> Fields marked as "Not used" must be omitted.
> — MG 8.2

Notes: OPC UA fields that MG 8.2 does not list are no user-defined keys (SF-050, resolved C-024); validators report a key that is defined neither by the guideline nor by OPC UA as an error of the sender in the strict validation mode; the tolerant mode ignores it (SF-052). The receiver side (tolerant reader) is REQ-MSG-046.

## REQ-MSG-002

**MessageType per Method and Resource**

The payload of a message with the Method Pub, Get, Set or Del is a NetworkMessage with MessageType "ua-data", except for the Resource Metadata, whose payload is a DataSetMetaData with MessageType "ua-metadata". Call and Reply use the Action message types (REQ-ACT-001).

- Keyword: MUST
- Levels: L1 MUST · L2 MUST · L3 MUST
- Domain: messaging · Applies to: publisher, requester, responder
- Refs: MG 8.1, MG 8.2.1, MG 8.2.2, MG 9.1
- Verification: schema, d7-validate
- Status: reviewed
- Inventory: MG-8.2.1-c829a1a5, MG-8.2.2-623d087a

> The MQTT payload for Data is an object of type NetworkMessage
> — MG 8.2.1

> Only ua-data is valid here.
> — MG 8.2.1

> The MQTT payload for Metadata is an object of type DataSetMetaData
> — MG 8.2.2

> Only ua-metadata is valid here.
> — MG 8.2.2

Notes: The MessageType per Method × Resource follows the templates of MG 9.1 (payload columns of matrix/method-resource.yaml follow in C-028).

## REQ-MSG-003

**Fields of the NetworkMessage**

A NetworkMessage (ua-data) contains MessageId, MessageType, PublisherId, ReplyTo and Messages; it contains the DataSetClassId as required by REQ-MSG-011 and never contains a WriterGroupName. DataSetClassId, if present, is a GUID string with separators (Part 6 5.4.2.7).

- Keyword: MUST
- Levels: L1 MUST · L2 MUST · L3 MUST
- Domain: messaging · Applies to: publisher
- Refs: MG 8.2.1, MG 8.1.4
- Verification: schema, d7-validate
- Status: reviewed
- Inventory: MG-8.1.4-21f73147, MG-8.2.1-00cfed6e, MG-8.2.1-824316e6

> Not used, the WriterGroupName is part of each DataSetMessage.
> — MG 8.1.4

Notes: The NetworkMessage has no WriterGroupName field (MG 8.2.1 lists only the fields it carries); the JsonNetworkMessageContentMask of MG 8.1.4 sets bit 6 WriterGroupName to 0. The WriterGroupName of each DataSetMessage is REQ-MSG-016, REQ-MSG-021 and REQ-MSG-024 (MG 8.2.3).

## REQ-MSG-004

**Fixed JsonNetworkMessageContentMask**

Every NetworkMessage (ua-data) is built with the fixed JsonNetworkMessageContentMask of MG 8.1.4: NetworkMessage header, DataSetMessage header, PublisherId and ReplyTo are always sent, SingleDataSetMessage and WriterGroupName are not set, DataSetClassId as required by REQ-MSG-011 (mask 0x3B with, 0x2B without DataSetClassId).

- Keyword: MUST
- Levels: L1 MUST · L2 MUST · L3 MUST
- Domain: messaging · Applies to: publisher
- Refs: MG 8.1.4
- Verification: schema, d7-validate
- Status: reviewed
- Inventory: MG-8.1.4-137fb8f0, MG-8.1.4-21f73147, MG-8.1.4-6b8106c4, MG-8.1.4-9f335012, MG-8.1.4-cadab2e2, MG-8.1.4-de4c90cd

> Therefore, the Open Industry 4.0 Alliance defines fixed content masks, which shall be used by all OI4 Alliance-compliant applications.
> — MG 8.1.4

> The NetworkMessage header must always be sent.
> — MG 8.1.4

> The DataSetMessage header must always be sent.
> — MG 8.1.4

> The PublisherId must always be sent.
> — MG 8.1.4

> This results in the value 0x3B (59) for NetworkMessages with DataSetClassId and 0x2B (43) for NetworkMessages without DataSetClassId.
> — MG 8.1.4

Notes: Content masks are not visible on the wire; a receiver checks the resulting field presence. A subscriber relies on these settings (MG-8.1.4-229ec879, informative).

## REQ-MSG-006

**PublisherId is ServiceType and unencoded Identification Link**

The PublisherId of a NetworkMessage and of a DataSetMetaData is "&lt;ServiceType>/&lt;AppId>" of the sending application, with the AppId as unencoded Identification Link (REQ-IL-005). For Pub it equals the ServiceType and the decoded AppId of the topic; for Get, Set and Del the topic contains the AppId of the addressed application (MG 7.3), so the PublisherId is that of the requesting application.

- Keyword: MUST
- Levels: L1 MUST · L2 MUST · L3 MUST
- Domain: messaging · Applies to: publisher
- Refs: MG 8.2.1, MG 8.2.2, MG 7.3
- Verification: schema, d7-validate
- Status: reviewed
- Inventory: MG-8.2.1-3a360801, MG-8.2.1-fd17f8ba, MG-8.2.2-009e2d99

> String consisting of ServiceType (see 7.2 ServiceType Element) and the unencoded Identification Link of the application (see 4 The Identification Link and 7.3 AppId Element) - separated by a “/”.
> — MG 8.2.1

> For Get, Set and Del, the topic contains the AppId of the addressed application (7.3 AppId Element), and the PublisherId is that of the requesting application.
> — MG 8.2.1

> For the methods Get, Set, and Del, the AppId of the destination that has to react to these methods must be chosen. For the Pub method, the AppId of the publisher of the data itself must be chosen.
> — MG 7.3

## REQ-MSG-007

**Format of the MessageId**

The MessageId of a NetworkMessage and of a DataSetMetaData is "&lt;unixTimestampInMs>-&lt;PublisherId>" (current Unix time in milliseconds, "-", PublisherId of the message); if needed for uniqueness, a counter is appended to the timestamp ("&lt;unixTimestampInMs>&lt;counter>-&lt;PublisherId>").

- Keyword: MUST
- Levels: L1 MUST · L2 MUST · L3 MUST
- Domain: messaging · Applies to: publisher
- Refs: MG 8.2.1, MG 8.2.2
- Verification: schema, d7-validate
- Status: reviewed
- Inventory: MG-8.2.1-4a8ac924, MG-8.2.1-81ca33dc, MG-8.2.2-2ed17728, MG-8.2.2-6fd35797

> The Open Industry 4.0 Alliance defines the type as a combination of the current timestamp in ms precision with the PublisherId.
> — MG 8.2.1

> In these cases, the application must guarantee the uniqueness by providing an additional parameter (e.g. MessageId = &lt;unixTimestampInMs>&lt;counter>-&lt;PublisherId>).
> — MG 8.2.1

## REQ-MSG-008

**MessageId is globally unique**

Every MessageId is globally unique: a publisher never sends two messages (ua-data or ua-metadata) with the same MessageId.

## REQ-MSG-009

**Consumers treat the MessageId as opaque**

A consumer does not derive information (e.g. time or sender) from the content of a MessageId; it only compares MessageIds as a whole, e.g. a ReplyTo with the MessageId of its request.

- Keyword: MUST NOT
- Levels: L1 MUST NOT · L2 MUST NOT · L3 MUST NOT
- Domain: messaging · Applies to: subscriber
- Refs: MG 8.2.1
- Verification: manual
- Status: reviewed
- Inventory: MG-8.2.1-35341d9b

> Consumers shall treat the MessageId as an opaque, unique string and shall not derive any information from its content.
> — MG 8.2.1

The DataSetClassId is a lower-case GUID string with separators.

- Keyword: MUST

Notes: Lower case: MG A2 lists all ids in lower case and Part 6 5.1.3 writes GUIDs in lower case; receivers compare case-insensitively (confirmed by the PO in the C-024 review). The key is in the MetaData (DataSetMetaDataType) of a DataSetMetaData (MG A2, SF-049 (g)).

## REQ-MSG-011

**DataSetClassId in the NetworkMessage**

A NetworkMessage for a resource with a predefined DataSetClassId (REQ-MSG-010) carries that DataSetClassId, for every Method (Pub, Get, Set, Del) and also if its Messages contain only helper DataSets (PaginationRequest, Pagination, Locale). A NetworkMessage for Data carries the publisher-defined DataSetClassId if all its DataSetMessages belong to the same DataSet class and it is known to the sender, and omits it otherwise; a Get or Set on Data or Metadata carries it only if the requester knows it (e.g. from the Metadata).

- Keyword: MUST
- Levels: L1 MUST · L2 MUST · L3 MUST
- Domain: messaging · Applies to: publisher, requester, responder
- Refs: MG 8.2.1, MG 8.1.4, MG A2, SF-048
- Verification: schema, d7-validate
- Status: reviewed
- Inventory: MG-8.1.4-9af6086d, MG-8.2.1-2650bc1d, MG-8.2.1-89331a41, MG-8.2.1-d28a278c

> A NetworkMessage must always carry the DataSetClassId of the resource addressed by the topic, if the resource has a predefined DataSetClassId (A2 Predefined DataSetClassIds for Resources of the Alliance).
> — MG 8.2.1

> For Data, a NetworkMessage must carry the publisher-defined DataSetClassId, if all its DataSetMessages belong to the same DataSet class (e.g. Pub/Data/&lt;Source>/&lt;Tag>), and must omit it otherwise
> — MG 8.2.1

> The DataSetClassId shall be present for all resources defined by the Open Industry 4.0 Alliance which have DataSetClassId.
> — MG 8.2.1

> Set, if the DataSetClassId is known (mandatory for resources defined by the Open Industry 4.0 Alliance, see A2 Predefined DataSetClassIds for Resources of the Alliance).
> — MG 8.1.4

Notes: SF-048 (resolved C-024). The Data rule can only be checked per message when the sender's Metadata is known (DataSetClassId of each DataSetWriterId); the reference check verifies the predefined ids.

## REQ-MSG-013

**Publisher-defined DataSetClassId is stable per structure**

A publisher-defined DataSetClassId identifies one DataSet structure: it stays the same as long as the structure does not change, also across restarts of the publisher, and a new DataSetClassId is used when the structure changes.

- Keyword: MUST
- Levels: L1 MUST · L2 MUST · L3 MUST
- Domain: messaging · Applies to: publisher
- Refs: MG 8.2.1
- Verification: d7-monitor, manual
- Status: reviewed
- Inventory: MG-8.2.1-512cf9a0, MG-8.2.1-c96f020d

> It identifies the structure of the DataSet and shall be stable as long as this structure does not change, also across restarts of the publisher.
> — MG 8.2.1

> If the structure changes, a new DataSetClassId shall be used.
> — MG 8.2.1

## REQ-MSG-015

**ReplyTo links a reaction to its trigger**

Every NetworkMessage and every DataSetMetaData contains ReplyTo. If the message is a reaction to another message (e.g. the answer to a Get, an Event caused by a Set), ReplyTo is the MessageId of the triggering message; otherwise ReplyTo is the empty string.

- Keyword: MUST
- Levels: L1 MUST · L2 MUST · L3 MUST
- Domain: messaging · Applies to: publisher
- Refs: MG 8.2.1, MG 8.2.2, MG 8.1.4
- Verification: schema, d7-test
- Status: reviewed
- Inventory: MG-8.2.1-0831035f, MG-8.2.1-1643990f, MG-8.2.1-a22f2f73, MG-8.2.1-e52d765b, MG-8.2.2-a9360e31

> If the NetworkMessage is a reaction to another message (e.g. a publication requested via Get, or an Event caused by a Set), the ReplyTo must contain the MessageId of the message which triggered it.
> — MG 8.2.1

> Otherwise, the ReplyTo must be an empty string.
> — MG 8.2.1

> If the DataSetMetaData is a reaction to another message (e.g. a publication requested via Get/Metadata), the ReplyTo contains the MessageId of the message which triggered it.
> — MG 8.2.2

Notes: The ReplyTo does not address a receiver; every subscriber of the topic may consume the reaction (MG-8.2.1-f58de567, informative).

## REQ-MSG-016

**Fields of the DataSetMessage**

A DataSetMessage contains DataSetWriterId, DataSetWriterName, WriterGroupName and Payload; it may contain SequenceNumber, MetaDataVersion or MinorVersion (REQ-MSG-018), Timestamp, Status (REQ-MSG-026) and MessageType (REQ-MSG-029); it never contains a PublisherId. SequenceNumber is a UInt32 that strictly increases per DataSetWriter, Timestamp a DateTime string (ISO 8601, Part 6 5.4.2.6).

- Keyword: MUST
- Levels: L1 MUST · L2 MUST · L3 MUST
- Domain: messaging · Applies to: publisher
- Refs: MG 8.2.3
- Verification: schema, d7-validate

## REQ-MSG-017

**Fixed JsonDataSetMessageContentMask**

Every DataSetMessage is built with the fixed JsonDataSetMessageContentMask of MG 8.1.4: DataSetWriterId, DataSetWriterName and WriterGroupName (empty string if the resource uses no Filter) are always sent, PublisherId never, SequenceNumber, Timestamp, Status, MessageType and MetaDataVersion or MinorVersion are optional, FieldEncoding1 = 0 and FieldEncoding2 = 1 (VerboseEncoding); the resulting mask is between 0xA41 and 0xA7F (with MetaDataVersion) or 0xE7D (with MinorVersion).

## REQ-MSG-019

**Reserved DataSetWriterIds of the helper DataSets**

A PaginationRequest uses DataSetWriterId 1, a Pagination 2, a Locale 3 and a Query 9. > — MG 8.2.3

## REQ-MSG-020

**Application DataSetWriterIds start at 10**

DataSetWriterId 0 is never used. The DataSetWriterIds 1 to 9 are reserved (1 to 3 and 9 helper DataSets, 4 to 8 Actions of the common services); an application assigns its own DataSetWriterIds from 10.

- Keyword: MUST NOT
- Levels: L1 MUST NOT · L2 MUST NOT · L3 MUST NOT

- Verification: schema, d7-validate

> — MG 8.2.3

> The DataSetWriterIds 4 to 8 are reserved for the Actions of the common services
> — MG 8.2.3

Notes: DataSetWriterId 9 is used by the generic helper DataSet Query since GL-ADR-020 (SF-069, SF-073, C-027 review; before it was reserved without a defined use); MG 8.4 reserves 4 to 7 for future common services.

## REQ-MSG-021

**One DataSetWriterId per resource, DataSetWriterName and WriterGroupName**

A publisher assigns its own DataSetWriterId to each combination of resource, DataSetWriterName and WriterGroupName it publishes; the DataSetWriterId is unique within the publisher, and the DataSetMetaData of a DataSetMessage carries the same DataSetWriterId. Exception: all PublicationList DataSetMessages of a publisher share one common DataSetWriterId and all SubscriptionList DataSetMessages another one.

- Keyword: MUST
- Levels: L1 MUST · L2 MUST · L3 MUST
- Domain: messaging · Applies to: publisher

- Status: reviewed

> — MG 8.2.3

> Exception: all DataSetMessages of the resource PublicationList of a publisher use one common DataSetWriterId, and all DataSetMessages of the resource SubscriptionList use another common DataSetWriterId, because each entry has the same DataSet (9.1.8 PublicationList, 9.1.9 SubscriptionList); the DataSetWriterId of the described publication is given in the payload of the entry.
> — MG 8.2.3

> It is unique within the scope of a publisher. The related DataSetMetaData (8.2.2 DataSetMetaData) to this DataSetMessage contains the same DataSetWriterId.
> — MG 8.2.3

Notes: The PublicationList/SubscriptionList exception was added in C-027 after GL-ADR-019 (SF-067 (a)).

**Consumers do not store DataSetWriterIds permanently**

A consumer does not rely on a DataSetWriterId across restarts of the publisher; after a restart it resolves the DataSetWriterId again, e.g. via PublicationList or via DataSetWriterName and WriterGroupName.

- Levels: L1 MUST NOT · L2 MUST NOT · L3 MUST NOT

## REQ-MSG-023

**DataSetWriterName is the unencoded Identification Link of the asset**

The DataSetWriterName of a DataSetMessage and of a DataSetMetaData is the unencoded Identification Link of the asset providing the information; if the topic contains a Source, the DataSetWriterName is the decoded Source.

The WriterGroupName of a DataSetMessage and of a DataSetMetaData is the Filter of the topic in its topic-encoded form (MG 7.7), and the empty string for resources without Filter (e.g. MAM, Health); for a DataSetMessage published on a topic without Filter it is the Filter that addresses this DataSet.

A DataSetMessage contains a Status only if the status is not Good; a missing Status means Good.

## REQ-MSG-031

**Payload fields use VerboseEncoding with RawData**

The fields of the DataSet in the Payload of a DataSetMessage are encoded with the JSON VerboseEncoding and the RawData option (DataSetFieldContentMask 0x20): each field is its plain JSON value without status, timestamps or type information; fields of the abstract DataType BaseDataType are an object with a Value field, multi-dimensional arrays an object with Value and Dimensions, and enumerations a string "&lt;EnumName>_&lt;EnumValue>". The encodings of FieldEncoding2 = 0 (Part 14 V1.04) are not used.

- Keyword: MUST (implicit, SF-035)

> — MG 8.2.3

> In Open Industry 4.0 Alliance context, only the bit RawData (bit 5) is set, which results in the value 0x20 (32).

> The encodings selected by FieldEncoding2 = 0 are deprecated in OPC UA Part 14 and shall not be used.

## REQ-MSG-046

**Receivers ignore unknown keys (tolerant reader)**

A receiver of a message (subscriber, Responder, Requestor receiving a response) ignores every key of a payload object that it does not know or does not use and processes the message as if the key were absent; an unknown key is no reason to reject the message, to answer with an error or to treat the message as erroneous.

- Keyword: SHOULD
- Levels: L1 SHOULD · L2 SHOULD · L3 SHOULD
- Domain: messaging · Applies to: subscriber, requester, responder
- Refs: MG 8, SF-052
- Verification: d7-test
- Status: reviewed
- Inventory: MG-8-0a821168, MG-8-1749b10b, MG-8-5503034d

> A receiver should be tolerant in what it accepts: it should ignore all keys of a received message that it does not know or does not use, and process the message as if these keys were absent.
> — MG 8

> An unknown key should not be a reason to reject a message or to treat it as erroneous.
> — MG 8

> A message can therefore be validated in two modes: strict validation reports every key that is not defined for the object (conformance of the sender), tolerant validation ignores such keys and checks only the defined keys (view of a tolerant receiver).
> — MG 8

Notes: PO decisions of the C-023 review (SF-052, resolved C-024) and of the C-024 review (SHOULD instead of MUST, two validation modes): strict in what is sent (REQ-MSG-001), tolerant in what is accepted. D7 injects messages with additional keys and expects the normal reaction. The validators offer both modes (D7 option, reference checks payload.Strict/payload.Tolerant, vector field mode): strict reports undefined keys as REQ-MSG-001 (REQ-ACT-003 for Action messages), tolerant checks only the defined keys.
